gitCommit.subject: Record the spot a custody audit was struck at, and stop a frozen value reading as live (#388)
gitCommit.body:
Record the spot a custody audit was struck at, and stop a frozen value reading as live (#388)

The operator saw two different figures for the same 25 bars on the vault screen:
header S$4,502.50, latest audit S$4,504.25.

NOT A DEFECT, AND THE PROOF IS REPRODUCIBLE. Both use the same kernel —
grams x spot x (1 + buyback_premium/100), rounded per holding then summed. Live
spot S$179.651174/g gives per-bar S$180.10 and a 25-bar total of S$4,502.50: the
header, to the cent. The audit's S$4,504.25 is 25 x S$180.17, implying spot
~S$179.72, about 7 cents a gram higher. A structural check agrees: both totals
are exact multiples of 25 x a clean 2dp per-bar figure, which they would not
both be if the two paths rounded differently.

The header is valued at PAGE LOAD (holdings are fetched once on mount; after a
sign only loadAudits() runs). The audit is valued AT SIGNING — minutes later,
because this one had a photo and a video to upload first. Gold moved 0.04% in
between.

TWO REAL GAPS BEHIND IT.

1. Nothing said the audit figure was historical. Two identically-formatted
   numbers inches apart, which is why it read as a contradiction. The customer
   sees the same pair on one screen: live summary at vault/page.tsx:282, audit
   line at :574.

2. vault_audits stored the dollar figure and discarded the spot that produced
   it, so an attestation could not be reconstructed or defended later.

The divergence itself stays — a signed attestation has to be frozen. That is the
2026-08-25 precedent, where the corrupted audit was ANNOTATED rather than
rewritten because amending it would destroy the record of what was attested.

WHAT SHIPS
- spot_sgd_per_g + spot_source ('recorded' | 'derived') on vault_audits.
- The snapshot now RETURNS the spot it valued at and the route persists that
  exact figure — never a re-read, which could be a different tick and would
  leave the stored attestation failing to reconcile with its own total.
- One shared qualifier (lib/vault/audit-spot.ts) renders on both surfaces, so
  the value always reads as point-in-time: "at S$179.72/g", or "value at
  signing" where no spot is on the record. Shared because a label duplicated
  across two surfaces drifts — exactly how `Combibar` survived on the packing
  screen for two months after the same rule was fixed in two other places.

THE BACKFILL IS SOLVED, NOT LOOKED UP — 8 of 15.
gold_price_history holds a DAILY SGD price and it does NOT reconcile: against
the 2026-09-01 seven-bar audit it reproduces S$1,254.54 where S$1,251.53 was
signed, S$3.01 out. A spot that fails to multiply back to the attested total
makes the record look internally inconsistent, which is worse than no spot.

So each value is the spot that reproduces the attested total EXACTLY, solved
from that customer's real holding composition — including the NULL-premium
products (2g Merlion, 5g PAMP Fortuna) that make a naive total/grams inversion
wrong. All 8 verified against live production rows using the database's own
arithmetic: recomputed = attested, to the cent, every one. Each lands within
0.7% of that day's market price.

7 STAY NULL, DELIBERATELY. Where the holding composition has since changed, the
composition at signing cannot be established and no honest value exists. That
test also excludes the 2026-08-01 105g / S$17,504.45 audit on its own with no
special-casing — it was struck against the grams bug and inverting it would
attach a plausible-looking spot to a figure already known to be wrong.

GUARDS, ALL MUTATION-CHECKED
- The 8 derived spots are replayed through the REAL valuation kernel against
  their production compositions, so the migration's central claim is machine-
  checked rather than asserted in a comment. A cross-check fails if a value is
  added to the SQL without a reconciliation case.
- All three explicit projections must name the new columns — a column a
  projection does not name is dropped silently, the shape that dropped
  parent_type_label this morning and seven columns from create_order_atomic for
  three months.
- The existing toEqual shape-lock in vault-audit.test.ts caught the new field
  and was GROWN to the new contract rather than loosened to toMatchObject, so it
  keeps catching the next one.
Mutations run: corrupting a derived spot, reverting the customer projection, and
re-reading spot instead of using the snapshot's each fail exactly their own test.

iOS: NO BUILD. No apps/ios-customer/**, no .swift, no server-authored spec (and
no spec READS anything changed — checked, not assumed), no bundled asset, no
content/**. Not a bare zero, though: My Vault is a WebView embed of the live PWA
/vault (WebViewURL.swift:34), so the customer-facing qualifier reaches iOS users
on their next load, with no build.

Migration applied to DEV and PROD and verified on both: columns present and
nullable, CHECK present, PROD 8 derived / 7 null, DEV untouched, re-run a no-op.

npm run verify green (574 files / 7456 tests, +1 file / +20).
